title: HTML Tags and Attributes
description: What an HTML element actually is: the shape of a tag, how nesting builds the page as a tree, the document skeleton, what attributes add, how block and inline differ, and why the tag you choose carries meaning.

title: Understanding Tags
description: A definition or a use case, four tags, one right answer. Sixty-four tags from the everyday ones to the genuinely niche. Race a one, two or three minute clock for a high score, or work through the whole bank untimed.

title: Match the Attribute
description: One tag, one job, four versions of it. Sixty-four questions on the attributes that make a tag do what you want, from href and src to radio groups, colspan and scope. Race a clock for a high score, or work through the bank untimed.

title: HTML Structure Trainer
description: Forty-three drag-and-drop problems that train you to arrange HTML elements in the correct order, following the same path as the class: boilerplate, tags, text, lists, links and images, then semantic layout.

title: File Paths
description: What a path actually is: directions from one file to another, how relative and absolute paths differ, how to resolve one by hand, and why a path in a stylesheet counts from somewhere different.

title: Resolving Paths
description: Read a project's folder tree and type the paths that reach the files. Twenty problems where the src, href and alt values are blank and you fill them in, from a single flat folder to structures several levels deep.

title: HTML Debugger
description: Click the parts of a broken HTML page where the mistakes are. Thirty problems from Beginner to Expert, mixing in more kinds of mistake as you go.

title: Inline, Internal, External
description: The three places CSS can live, explained through annotated code. External, internal and inline side by side, with the comments in the code doing half the teaching, and a plain account of which one wins.

title: CSS Properties
description: What a CSS property actually is: the shape of a declaration, the kinds of value it accepts, how shorthands expand, what happens to properties you never set, and how to name values of your own.

title: Complete the CSS
description: Read what the design needs, then type the missing property or value into the blank. Forty problems across text and colour, the box model, backgrounds and borders, and layout, with a preview that updates as you type.

title: Match the CSS
description: Read a real CSS snippet, then pick which of five live previews it actually produces. Forty questions across single HTML elements and whole-page layouts, running from obvious to easy to miss.

title: CSS Selectors
description: What a CSS selector actually is: a pattern that picks out elements, how simple selectors combine, how pseudo-classes match a state, and how specificity settles a conflict between two rules.

title: Write the Selector
description: The CSS is written for you but the selector is missing. Read the page, then write a selector that reaches exactly the outlined elements. Thirty problems across basic selectors, combinators, pseudo-classes and attributes.

title: How Browsers Parse HTML and CSS
description: Step through a browser's parser one token at a time and watch it build the DOM tree, the CSSOM tree and the render tree in real time.
